s: A company runs production workloads on EC2 On-Demand Instances and RDS for PostgreSQL. They want to reduce costs without compromising availability or capacity.
o: Use CUR and Lambda to terminate underutilized instances. Buy Savings Plans.
Use Budgets and Trusted Advisor, then manually terminate and buy RIs.
Use Compute OptimizerandTrusted Advisor for recommendations. Apply rightsizing, auto scaling, and purchase a Compute Savings Plan.
Use Cost Explorer, alerts, and replace with Spot Instances.
e: C is correct:AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze usage patterns and recommends rightsizing. Trusted Advisor adds further insights. Combining these with Savings Plans gives the best cost optimization without reducing availability. A is risky due to using Lambda for termination. B and D offer partial or manual solutions. Reference:AWS Compute Optimizer

w.y: Reduce cost without hurting availability or capacity. Compute Optimizer and Trusted Advisor find right-sizing opportunities, auto scaling matches capacity to demand, and a Compute Savings Plan discounts the steady compute usage while keeping it On-Demand reliable.

o.A: Automatically terminating instances can harm availability of production workloads.
o.B: Manual work with Budgets is slow, and Budgets gives no right-sizing recommendations.
o.C: Correct: right-sizing, auto scaling, and a Compute Savings Plan cut cost without risking capacity.
o.D: Spot Instances can be interrupted, which risks production availability.
